messages:
incident-bot:  PAGING: synthetic-infer-canary failures firing (noise) and elevated 5xx from us-east-1 observed concurrently. AlertGroup: inference.synthetic, alert_count=4. Pager policy applied.

SRE Bot: paging @Devon H (oncall) and notifying #eng-oncall. Runbook link: /runbooks/inference-paging.md

Devon H: I have the pager. quick sanity checks: recent deploys? config changes? synthetic job config?

Noah R: no infra deploys in last 6h. I see the synthetic canary job shifted its region target to us-east-1 at 02:10 UTC due to a scheduler change. Canary now runs 10x per minute (bug). That explains the synthetic alert noise.

Zara M: while investigating, noticed real traffic p95 rising ~400ms and a small bump in 5xx ~0.8% for ~6m. Might be autoscaler thrash on inference-pool-2.

Casey L: autoscaler thrash? any OOMs or pod restarts?

Noah R: yes, kube events show repeated scale-up then down over last 7m and kubelet evicts on one node due to ephemeral storage pressure.

Devon H: mitigation plan: 1) quiet synthetic alerts and fix canary schedule, 2) pin canary to a separate job/label so it doesn't contribute to global metrics, 3) increase min replicas for inference-pool-2 to avoid thrash, 4) open customer-impact ticket if 5xx persists. I'll start 1 and 3 now.

Ops Eng: commands ready:
```bash
# silence synthetic alerting rule for 30m
rwdctl alerts mute inference.synthetic --duration 30m --reason "noisy canary"
# bump min replicas
kubectl scale deployment inference-pool-2 --replicas=6 -n redwood
```

Devon H: ran both commands. synthetic alerts muted. replicas now 6.

SRE Bot: system note: incidents.quiet applied to inference.synthetic for 30m by Devon H.

Zara M: after scaling, p95 back to normal in ~4m, 5xx down to 0.2%. Good.

Devon H: status check: synthetic alert noise was the root cause of initial pager. But we had real impact due to autoscaler + node disk pressure. We need both alert tuning and infra guardrails.

Casey L: agree. Proposed alert changes (short):
- Split synthetic and production metrics at ingestion (label: source=synthetic).
- Synthetic alerts -> ticket only (no page) unless they coincide with production-impact label.
- Production 5xx alert: raise from 1% over 2m to 1.25% over 4m, but add label 'impacting_customers=true' if requests from known account ranges have >0.5% 5xx, which should page immediately.

Noah R: example modified rule for production 5xx:
```yaml
alert: ProductionInference5xx
expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\",source!=\"synthetic\",status=~\"5..\"}[4m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\",source!=\"synthetic\"}[4m])) > 0.0125
for: 4m
labels:
  severity: ticket
annotations:
  runbook: /runbooks/inference-5xx
```
and a companion rule to page when impacted accounts hit threshold:
```yaml
alert: Inference5xx_AccountImpact
expr: sum by (account) (rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\",status=~\"5..\"}[2m])) / sum by (account) (rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\"}[2m])) > 0.005
for: 1m
labels:
  severity: page
```

Devon H: good. Also want alert routing changes: map severity.page -> escalate to oncall+eng-sre for P1 incidents, severity.ticket -> create issue in #eng-ops. Also add a special mapping: severity.synthetic -> create ticket only in #devex.

Zara M: UX request: add dashboard panels '5xx by source (prod/synthetic)', 'min replicas by pool', and 'ephemeral_storage pressure by node'. That will reduce guesswork during triage.

Casey L: ops task: enforce node ephemeral-storage alert at node-level earlier (e.g., warn at 60% usage). Might have prevented eviction.

Devon H: temporal handoff: I'll monitor for 45m and then hand to next oncall. Please capture action items.

Noah R: filing infra tickets: INF-1201 (split synthetic/production metrics), INF-1202 (raise prod 5xx threshold + add account-impact rule), INF-1203 (node storage early warning). Assigning to @Noah R and @Casey L.

Zara M: I'll add the dashboard PR GRAF-990 and link in tickets.

incident-bot: Note: create post-incident review? Use /incident create to generate PIR.

Devon H: creating PIR. Owner: Devon H. Brief summary in PIR: noisy synthetic canary + autoscaler node disk pressure led to short-lived customer impact; mitigated by silencing synthetic alerts and increasing min replicas. Draft due tomorrow EOD.

Casey L: follow-ups to include: 1) change canary scheduling defaults, 2) metric-labeling at ingestion, 3) alert routing changes + mapping table, 4) autoscaler stabilization policy (min/max tweaks), 5) node ephemeral storage monitoring and k8s eviction tuning.

Devon H: ok closing pager. Thanks team. Handing over to SRE Bot for quiet window checks and follow-up enforcement. :white_check_mark:

SRE Bot: acknowledged. Will re-evaluate mute at 30m and run periodic checks on the indicated metrics.

Ops Eng: customer-impact? No high volume customers reported errors beyond a tiny set (<5 accounts) with retries auto-succeeded. No active data loss.

Devon H: thanks. if anything else crop up, re-open the thread.
